corpus.title: Former gang member found guilty of murdering Tupac Shakur
corpus.signal_text:
World News
Duane "Keffe D" Davis, a former Los Angeles gang leader, was found guilty on Monday by a Las Vegas court of the 1996 murder of chart-topping rapper Tupac Shakur.
Thirty years after the rap legend's death, the jury found Davis, 63, guilty of murder after just a few hours of deliberation.
"Count one, murder with use of a deadly weapon, guilty of first-degree murder with use of a deadly weapon," the foreperson of the jury announced to the court.
Davis, who faces possible life in prison without parole, addressed Judge Carli Kierny after the verdict was announced and stated his intention to appeal.
The one-time leader of the South Side Compton Crips was accused of ordering the September 7, 1996 killing of the hip-hop artist after his own nephew had been beaten by members of Shakur's entourage at a Las Vegas casino.
"Duane Davis, in the culture of gangs, could not let that stand," prosecutor Binu Palal said during closing arguments. "So what did he do? He acquired a firearm, got his group together, and went hunting for Mr Shakur."
Shakur, who was in Las Vegas for a Mike Tyson heavyweight fight, was shot about two hours after the casino confrontation by a gunman in a white Cadillac that pulled up at a red light alongside the BMW in which the rapper was riding in the front passenger seat.
According to prosecutors, Davis handed the gun to someone sitting in the back seat of the Cadillac and ordered that person to shoot Shakur, who died six days later.
Davis is the only person who was in the Cadillac that evening who is still alive.
The driver of the BMW, Death Row Records co-founder Marion "Suge" Knight, was wounded.
The killing of Shakur, also known as 2Pac, has been one of America's most famous cold cases, prompting endless debate among music fans over who did it, and why.
Davis, whose Crips were one of a patchwork of rival gangs that ran parts of Los Angeles in the 1990s, is the only person to have been charged in connection with the shooting of Shakur.
Sentencing is scheduled for October 13.
Confession
The investigation into Shakur's murder sputtered for decades because of a lack of evidence, but the case was revived when Davis's memoirs were published in 2019.
In that book, Davis recounted that he was in the front seat of the Cadillac and that he handed a pistol to those in the back seat. But he does not say who opened fire on Shakur.
Davis has repeatedly boasted over the years of involvement in Shakur's murder -- in interviews with law enforcement

corpus.title: Tupac Shakur verdict: 'Duane 'Keffe D' Davis found guilty in 1996 murder
corpus.signal_text:
Published September 01, 2026
Duane “Keffe D” Davis has been found guilty of orchestrating Tupac Shakur’s 1996 murder, bringing a nearly 30-year-old mystery to a close.
Following a 2-week trial, a 12-person jury reached the verdict Monday, August 31, after less than three hours of deliberation, according to the Associated Press.
Davis, 63, was convicted of murder with the use of a deadly weapon in connection with the drive-by shooting that killed Shakur at the height of his career.
Shakur was shot in Las Vegas on September 7, 1996, while riding in a BMW driven by Death Row Records co-founder Marion “Suge” Knight.
During the trial, which was live-streamed, prosecutors argued that the attack was retaliation for an earlier confrontation at the MGM Grand, where Shakur and his entourage were involved in a fight with Davis’ nephew, Orlando “Baby Lane” Anderson.
Davis was riding in the white Cadillac from which the shots were fired, alongside Anderson and two other men. Prosecutors did not accuse Davis of pulling the trigger, but alleged that he organised the killing and supplied the firearm.
Shakur died from his injuries six days later, on September 13, 1996. The case remained unsolved for decades until Davis was arrested in September 2023.
His 2019 memoir, Compton Street Legend, and past interviews became key pieces of the prosecution’s case. Davis’ attorney Michael Sanft, however, dismissed his previous claims as “bulls***” in his opening statements.
Davis plans to appeal. His sentencing is scheduled for October 13.
